items.evidence: apiLevel 2.13, p20 used for 1-20 uL and p300 for ≥20 uL (106, 40, 250 uL; 30 uL mixes), no overfilled wells, and all simulator checks pass.

tip_before_aspirate, tip_dropped_at_end and no_cross_contamination all pass. Fresh tips are used per primer, template, chromoprotein fragment and eluate, and shared reagents are dispensed with one tip.

The code transfers the whole 10 uL eluate to the cells (p20.transfer(ASSEMBLY_ELUTION,...)) and skips the NanoDrop 5 uL aliquot. The paper transforms about 5 uL and keeps 5 uL for quantification, and end_state shows assembly_plate 10 vs 15 and cells_plate 310 vs 305.

Master mix is 13.25 water + 5 buffer + 0.5 dNTP + 0.25 polymerase per reaction (19 uL). Each well then gets 2.5+2.5 uL primers and 1 uL template, with the primer and template mapping from the design table, giving 25 uL.

The PCR comment records 98 C 30 s, 34 cycles of 98 C 10 s, annealing 30 s and 72 C, then 72 C 5 min. DpnI is 19 uL water + 5 uL rCutSmart + 1 uL DpnI, then 37 C 30 min and 65 C 20 min, followed by a clean-up pause, in that order.
Each assembly well gets 7 uL water, 2 uL T4 buffer, fragments 3/2/3/2 uL per the design table and 1 uL enzyme mix, totalling 20 uL in A1:D1.

The comment gives a Golden Gate program of 30 cycles of 37 C/16 C, then 60 C and a 4 C hold. Clean-up elutes in 10 uL, and the eluate goes into the cells with 30 min on ice, 42 C 60 s, 250 uL LB+dextrose, 37 C 60 min recovery and kanamycin plating.

judge.summary: The protocol is sound and nearly faithful: the PCR, DpnI, assembly and Golden Gate steps match the paper and the design table, and all tip and safety checks pass. It fails fidelity because it transforms the entire 10 uL eluate and skips the NanoDrop aliquot, where the paper transforms about 5 uL and keeps 5 uL.
